title: Turkey, light and dark meat, roasted, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a large poultry bird raised mainly for its meat. Light meat (breast) is lower in fat and calories, while dark meat (thighs, drumsticks) is richer, juicier, and more flavorful. Roasted meat without skin retains most nutrients and works well in a variety of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is a national symbol in the United States, especially on Thanksgiving.
Light meat contains about 30 % fewer calories than dark meat.
Dark meat is higher in iron and zinc compared with breast meat.
Roasting without skin reduces saturated fat while preserving flavor through natural juices.
Turkey belongs to the pheasant family and is closely related to chickens.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Turkey meat provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat in breast meat
items.content: Skin‑less breast meat is very low in saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey is rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Dark meat especially supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Very low carbohydrate
items.content: Turkey contains virtually no carbs, fitting well into low‑carb eating plans.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey meat.

items.title: Handling and storage
items.content: Improper storage of roasted turkey can allow bacterial growth leading to foodborne illness.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: If the turkey is seasoned with salt or sauces, sodium levels can become high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted, skin‑less turkey can be sliced for salads, sandwiches, pastas, or used as a base for soups. Breast strips work well for quick meals, while dark meat adds heartiness to stews and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep roasted turkey in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it retains quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
